main_issue: How to share the single window corner of the living room among A's permanent desk, C's laundry rack, B's weekend seating, and D's prayer space

A-B.evidence: B proposes a folding desk and helping pack it (T12, T15); A refuses repeatedly (T16, T22); B says the room can't be one person's office (T23).

A-C.evidence: C asks where the laundry rack goes if the desk is permanent (T24, T26); A replies the rack needn't move (T25), but C says it is already tight.

A-D.evidence: D notes a permanent desk leaves no space for the prayer mat (T19); A does not accommodate, and D proposes clearing the corner (T27) which A has not accepted.

B-C.evidence: C backs B: 'He's right. If your desk is permanent, where does my laundry rack go?' (T24).

B-D.evidence: Both oppose a permanent desk (T17-T19, T23); D's earlier prayer-needs reply (T5) was in tension with B's weekend seating, but both ended up broadly aligned against the desk.

C-D.evidence: C asks where D's things would go (T26); D thanks C and says 'That's the problem' (T27).
